title: TREATMENT OF ACNE IN ADULT WOMEN
official:
AFTER - Treatment of women with Acne vulgaris - Evaluation of the eFficacy of isoTretinoin low-dose vs spironolactonE in the attack phase and spiRonolactone in the maintenance phase: 
A 2-step randomized controlled trial
summary:
Main objective: 1) Demonstrate the superiority of isotretinoin low-dose in comparison to spironolactone in attack phase treatment on the clinical severity and on improving quality of life.
2) Demonstrate the superiority of spironolactone in treatment maintenance phase after clinical success (in the patients from the attack phase) in comparison to usual topical maintenance care.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. - Woman ≥ 25 years. - Woman with facial acne (mandibular or diffuse) for at least six months.  - Patient having already received 3 months of cyclines in the 2 years preceding inclusion. - Woman with failed or recurrent facial acne after treatment with cyclines or who have experienced an adverse reaction during treatment with cyclines for acne. - Patient with mild, moderate or severe acne (GEA score 2, 3 or 4)  - Patient on effective contraception ≥ 1 month. - Subject is able to comprehend and willing to sign an Informed Consent. - Affiliation to French social coverage.
Exclusion criteria:
1. - Patient with a GEA score 1 and with GEA score 5- Past cure of oral isotretinoin in the last 12 months.- Past cure of systemic antibiotics for acne in the last 3 months Past cure of anti-androgens in the 6 months preceding inclusion (excluding progestative or oestroprogestative contraception). - Contraindicated to spironolactone:  	- patient with known intolerance or hypersensitivity to spironolactone 	- severe or acute renal insufficiency            - Estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60ml/ min/1.73 m2.           - Patient with hyperkalaemia or requiring potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g., amiloride, canrenoate, eplerenone, triamterene) or treated continuously with ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II antagonist, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), heparin and low molecular weight heparin, ciclosporin, tacrolimus and trimethoprim. - Association with potassium salts  - Concomitant treatment with mitotane - Androgen-secreting adrenal or ovarian tumour. Cushing’s syndrome. - Congenital adrenal hyperplasia, Addison’s disease.  - End-stage liver disease.- Contraindicated to oral isotretinoin:  	- patient with known intolerance or hypersensitivity to isotretinoin - pregnant or breast-feeding women. 	- impaired liver function.  - elevated blood lipid levels (cholesterol and triglycerides) 	- hypervitaminosis A, concomitant vitamin A supplementation 	- association with tetracyclines.
